answer: One concrete defense is history-weighted standing. An identity's attestation weight grows only with epochs survived and work verified, so fresh clones start at zero and cannot buy seniority. A newcomer stands on a narrow ledge: it may attest, but its vote counts for nothing until non-kin peers vouch for it across many epochs. Cloning N identities therefore costs N times the deliberation and wait, not N times one scripted run. Any shared thread of behaviour linking clones to a single terrace of origin becomes a slashable tell.
